facts.statement: The genus Noguerornis was described by Lacasa-Ruiz in 1989.
Noguerornis belongs to the extinct avian clade Enantiornithes.
Noguerornis lived approximately 130 million years ago during the early Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It lived during the Early Cretaceous (early Barremian age) about 130 mya

facts.statement: The species lived during the early Barremian stage of the Lower Cretaceous, about 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vivió durante el Cretácico inferior (Barremiense temprano), hace unos 130 millones de años

facts.statement: The fossil record for Noguerornis spans from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago within the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Noguerornis have been found in the La Pedrera de Rúbies Formation at El Montsec, Spain.
facts.quote: is known from fossils found in the La Pedrera de Rúbies Formation at El Montsec, Spain

facts.statement: The genus is known from fossils discovered in the La Pedrera de Rúbies Formation in El Montsec, Spain.
facts.quote: se conoce a partir de fósiles hallados en la Formación La Pedrera de Rúbies en El Montsec, España

facts.statement: Noguerornis gonzalezi is the type species for the genus Noguerornis.
The only known species in the genus is Noguerornis gonzalezi.
The species Noguerornis gonzalezi was named by Lacasa-Ruiz in 1989.
Researchers suggest that Noguerornis may be related to the genus Iberomesornis.
Noguerornis is a member of the Enantiornithes clade and is possibly related to Iberomesornis.
facts.quote: perteneciente al clado Enantiornithes y posiblemente emparentada con Iberomesornis
